content.page_summary: Guidance on management of acute pulmonary embolism (PE), focusing on advanced life support in cardiac arrest and initial anticoagulation strategies.
content.6.1.4_Advanced_life_support_in_cardiac_a: Acute PE should be considered in differential diagnosis of cardiac arrest with non-shockable rhythm. Follow current advanced life support guidelines; consider thrombolytic therapy and continue CPR for at least 60–90 minutes after thrombolytic administration before terminating attempts.
content.6.2_Initial_anticoagulation: Recommendations for initiating anticoagulation in patients with high or intermediate clinical probability of PE while awaiting diagnostic tests.
content.6.2.1_Parenteral_anticoagulation: Use subcutaneous, weight-adjusted LMWH or fondaparinux, or IV unfractionated heparin (UFH). LMWH and fondaparinux preferred over UFH due to lower bleeding and HIT risk. UFH reserved for haemodynamic instability, imminent reperfusion, serious renal impairment (CrCl <30 mL/min) or severe obesity. Dosing adjustments based on CrCl and aPTT monitoring for UFH.
content.6.2.2_Non-vitamin_K_antagonist_oral_anti: NOACs directly inhibit single activated coagulation factors: dabigatran inhibits thrombin; apixaban, edoxaban and rivaroxaban inhibit factor Xa. Phase III trials support single-oral drug strategies (e.g., higher-dose apixaban or rivaroxaban) for acute PE.
content.additional_notes: LMWH/fondaparinux do not require routine anti-Xa monitoring; use of NOACs benefits from predictable bioavailability and pharmacokinetics allowing fixed dosing without routine laboratory monitoring.

Associated Conditions: Anticoagulation therapy for acute pulmonary embolism (PE)
